bottomLine: The biggest themes right now are inflation, trade policy and interest rates. This briefing is put together automatically from headlines and market data, and the bullish or bearish ratings come from keyword rules, so read the linked articles before drawing conclusions.

stories.headline: Falling oil prices are no longer enough to bring down borrowing costs in the world’s most important bond market
stories.what: The tight trading relationship between oil prices and Treasury yields has broken down. It’s a sign that inflation concerns are extending beyond the energy shock.
stories.why: Inflation readings shape what the Fed does next: hotter numbers pressure stocks and bonds, cooler ones support them.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang affair in D.C.: Resignation calls and moves to tighten Nvidia China exports
stories.what: Huang was notably opposed to strict export controls on AI chips to China, which ruffled feathers with congressional China hawks.
stories.why: Trade policy changes costs and access to markets for exporters and importers, which can hit earnings across sectors.

stories.headline: Fed's Goolsbee calls inflation report 'borderline disturbing' as central bank weighs more hikes
stories.what: The consumer price index rose more than expected in October, raising alarm among Federal Reserve officials.
stories.why: Interest rate expectations feed straight into stock valuations and borrowing costs, so central bank news tends to move the whole market.

stories.headline: CoreWeave beats on revenue and lifts guidance, easing AI slowdown concerns
stories.what: CoreWeave's stock has been hammered heading into the neocloud's Q3 earnings report.
stories.why: Earnings and guidance show how companies are really doing, which moves their shares and can set the tone for their sector.

stories.headline: Social Security could pay full benefits until 2059 if taxable payroll kept pace with GDP: AARP report
stories.what: An aging work force is not the only reason Social Security's trust funds now have a looming shortfall, according to AARP Public Policy Institute research.
stories.why: The job market drives consumer spending and Fed policy, so labor data can shift rate expectations and stock prices.

stories.headline: Nasdaq futures fall as Nvidia sinks 8% after hours on report board may oust Huang
stories.what: Stock futures were sliding Wednesday evening as a selloff in shares of Nvidia after the closing bell weighed on the Nasdaq-100 and dragged down shares of other chip makers.
stories.why: AI and chip stocks are a large part of the major indexes, so big moves in the group sway the whole market.

stories.headline: Nvidia prepares to oust Jensen Huang, WSJ reports, stock sinks
stories.what: The report comes days after Huang admitted to an affair with a woman who is believed by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
stories.why: Broad market moves show how investors are pricing the latest news and set the tone for the next session.

stories.headline: CoreWeave just gave a shot in the arm to Micron, Lumentum and the rest of the AI trade
stories.what: CoreWeave’s improved AI economics and its vow to show some discipline around debt are sparking a broad rally across the chip sector.
stories.why: AI and chip stocks are a large part of the major indexes, so big moves in the group sway the whole market.

stories.headline: Nissan cuts sales forecast again on China woes as CEO outlines plan to fight back
stories.what: Intensifying competition in the world's largest auto market forced Nissan to cut its annual sales forecast for a second time in months.
stories.why: Earnings and guidance show how companies are really doing, which moves their shares and can set the tone for their sector.

stories.headline: Alibaba announces plans to list T-Head, its Nvidia chip rival
stories.what: Alibaba noted it had already filed confidentially on Sept. 11 to list T-Head on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
stories.why: AI and chip stocks are a large part of the major indexes, so big moves in the group sway the whole market.
